title: EUNIS habitat classification (revised 2021/2022 and 2012)
publisher: European Environment Agency (EEA); served by the Biodiversity Information System for Europe (BISE)
version: Revised classification 2021/2022 (terrestrial 2021, marine 2022) plus EUNIS 2012 for the groups not yet revised (C, J, X) and the 2012 codes still used for urban greens; each entry names its generation in version
license_note: Codes and names from the BISE hierarchical views (2021/2022: https://biodiversity.europa.eu/resources/search-habitat/eunis-habitat-types-hierarchical-view-2021-2022; 2012: https://biodiversity.europa.eu/resources/search-habitat/eunis-habitat-types-hierarchical-view-2012). The classification defines no colours. Colours exist only for 2012 level 1 and 2 codes, from the legend of the EEA map 'Ecosystem types of Europe' v3.1 (map service Ecosystem/EcosystemTypeMap_v3_1_Terrestrial); they were sampled from the legend swatch images (evidence V*).
note: Two code generations in one file: 2012 codes have a dot after the second character (E2.64, FA.3), the 2021/2022 codes have none (V31, R22); their level-1 letters do not overlap (2012: A-J, X; 2021: M, MH, MJ, N, Q, R, S, T, U, V). Inland waters (C), constructed habitats (J) and habitat complexes (X) are not revised, so their 2012 codes are current. The prefix fallback resolves deeper codes to their group (E2.66 -> E2.6 -> E2 -> E). Level-3 selections for R, S, T, Q, U and N cover temperate urban and peri-urban types only; other codes fall back to their level-2 group. EUNIS is the only European scheme that separates lawn (V31, E2.64, E2.65), meadow (R22, E2.2) and species-rich or ruderal stands; the 2012 -> 2021 correspondence is not encoded here. Names that the research gives in shorthand (C1.1-C1.4, C3.7, E5.13, E5.14, J5.1, J5.2, Q61, Q62, X13-X16) were completed from the shared wording of their sibling codes. Legend colours collide for D5/F6 and D6/F7.
